summary: Kixx was U.S. Gold's budget-price re-release label, returning established computer games to the shelves at a lower price across the late 1980s and 1990s.
facts: MobyGames identifies Kixx as a budget-price label of U.S. Gold and records the label from the late 1980s into the 1990s.
The Mastertronic Collectors Archive records that U.S. Gold created Kixx after previously supplying older full-price titles to third-party budget ranges.
Preserved Kixx releases include Commodore 64 and Amiga titles as well as releases on other home-computer formats.
note: Kixx is shown by CCG as a re-release publisher when a game record credits the label in its re-release field; the original publisher credit remains intact.

sources.label: Mastertronic Collectors Archive — republished software labels

summary: The Hit Squad became Ocean Software's major budget re-release label, bringing Ocean's own back catalogue and selected third-party titles back to market at lower prices.
facts: MobyGames identifies The Hit Squad as a budget label of Ocean Software and records releases under the label across the late 1980s and 1990s.
The label was used not only for Ocean software but also for titles originally associated with publishers including Domark, Activision, Electronic Arts, Taito and Virgin.
The Centre for Computing History preserves Hit Squad editions on Commodore 64 and Amiga alongside releases for other home computers.
note: The Hit Squad is shown by CCG as a re-release publisher when a game record credits the label in its re-release field; the original publisher credit remains intact.

sources.label: Centre for Computing History — The Hit Squad catalogue
